A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FoNE research. All 28 pages of v1 and 32 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original arithmetic experiments, efficiency measurements, ablations, binary classification, Fourier analyses, 60-digit addition and Abacus generalization results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds language-model pretraining, continual pretraining, modular arithmetic, base-sensitivity experiments and Number Token Loss comparisons.

M1.justification: The core Fourier encoder, digit-classification loss and decoder remain unchanged. Section 5 adds a simplified adaptation that computes FoNE for existing BPE numerical subwords and learns a projection into pretrained token-embedding space during continual pretraining. This changes the integration procedure without redesigning the core method.

E1.justification: v2 expands beyond the original predominantly synthetic evaluation to FineWeb language modeling and MegaMath-Web-Pro continual pretraining, with MMLU and zero-shot arithmetic evaluation. Appendix B adds modular addition and base-5 inputs; Appendix E.1 adds direct-prompting scenarios for production LLMs. The original binary-classification, 60-digit addition and Abacus tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Appendix K introduces substantial head-to-head comparisons against Number Token Loss with digit-wise and subword tokenization, each evaluated at three loss weights across two arithmetic tasks and multiple data sizes. Original comparators remain. The five production LLMs in Table 9 are evaluated separately, rather than in a matched comparison against FoNE.

E3.justification: New protocols include paired continual pretraining on 15B tokens and GPT-2–117M pretraining on 10B FineWeb tokens. Appendix K specifies an eight-layer, 512-dimensional model, 50 training epochs, varying training-set sizes and 1,000 held-out examples evaluated with accuracy, R2 and RMSE. Appendix E.1 adds two-shot, temperature-zero testing on 100 sampled problems per setting. The original arithmetic split and configuration tables are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B extends the original period ablation with a base-7-to-13 sweep and tests matching FoNE periods to base-5 inputs. Appendix K analyzes sensitivity to NTL loss weights. Section 5 adds a targeted text-only perplexity analysis on sequences containing both text and numbers, examining possible interference with language modeling. Original ablations and generalization analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three random-seed runs for the Abacus comparison. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting procedures for its new experiments. The 100-problem samples in Appendix E.1 describe evaluation sample sizes, not repeated training runs.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results, while v2 adds substantial new findings. Table 4 reports 59.00% versus 51.35% four-digit addition accuracy for simplified FoNE versus the regular model, with MMLU scores of 38.21% versus 38.10%. Table 5 reports text-only perplexity of 46.856 for FoNE versus 67.390 for BPE. Table 16 reports 89.3% multiplication accuracy for FoNE versus 16.3% for the best NTL variant at 75K samples. These are newly reported comparisons under added protocols.

T1.justification: The mathematical encoding, loss and prediction definitions and the recovery and normalization proofs are substantively retained, with v1 Appendix C becoming v2 Appendix D. Former Lemma 3.5 appears as explanatory prose in Section 3.2 with the same reasoning. The added positional-encoding discussion introduces no new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The central single-token representation, efficiency, perfect-arithmetic-accuracy and 64-fold data-efficiency claims remain. v2 explicitly scopes the introductory perfect-accuracy claim to Transformers trained from scratch and highlights the existing 38M-versus-fine-tuned-1B comparison in the abstract. The conclusion more cautiously frames broader downstream applications as future research.

C2.justification: v1 treats integration with pretrained LLMs as future work; v2 interprets its new MMLU and perplexity experiments as evidence that FoNE preserves or improves semantic abilities. It also adds substantive arguments about classification versus regression, alternative numerical embeddings, positional encodings, numeral-base alignment and NTL loss weighting. Some interpretations overstate the evidence: Appendix B describes period 8 as performing poorly on base-5 inputs, whereas Table 7 reports 99.97% accuracy.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies that digit limits are global hyperparameters, describes numeric-string parsing, distinguishes scratch training from the fine-tuned baseline, and adds training-time bounds and NTL implementation settings. Most original configuration details remain. However, v1's code-and-visualization access link is removed, as is its blanket A6000 hardware statement; A6000 details remain for the long-number and Abacus experiments.

R1.justification: The Fourier-based numeracy positioning remains, with targeted additions concerning NTL/regression losses, SALSA, sinusoidal positional encodings and newer numerical-representation and frequency-bias studies. The original Fourier-related-work discussion is moved to Appendix C and expanded. These changes refine the relationship to prior work without fundamentally redefining the contribution.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: it rewrites the abstract and discussion, separates representational properties into Section 3.2, moves algorithms to Appendix A, and relocates the existing Abacus and long-number discussions into Section 4.4. It also replaces the appendix roadmap with a contents page and adds reproducibility and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: v2 combines an encoder illustration with the original decimal-addition results in Figure 1, redraws main performance plots using logarithmic error axes, and adds a new integration diagram in Figure 2. The original pipeline becomes Figure 6, Figure 4's panels are reordered, and table layouts are reformatted. New language-modeling and NTL figures and multiple experimental tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 largely supports its proposed usefulness for language models through synthetic tasks and leaves pretrained integration for future work. v2 substantially addresses this validation gap with actual continual-pretraining/MMLU experiments and 10B-token FineWeb training, including text-only perplexity evaluation. The NTL comparisons also strengthen assessment against an alternative numerical-learning approach. These gains outweigh the removed code-access pointer and new reporting inconsistencies, such as the conflict between Appendix B's period-8 description and Table 7, although uncertainty reporting remains limited.
